text:
alex: Heads-up — noticed a 12% CPU regression on our small-token streams after the kernel-selector warmup change; perf + flamegraph attached in thread.

maria: oof. Which workload? cold start or steady-state?

alex: Mostly cold-start bursts (short requests, 8-32 tokens). Warmup path picks an 'optimized' kernel that expects long sequences; that increases Python scheduler churn and tokenization time.

sam: can you paste the perf top / stackcollapse bits? curious if GIL or tokenizer is the dominant hot path.

alex: quick excerpt from perf script stackcollapse (trimmed):

```
python3;_tokenize_bytes;_tokenize_bytes+0x1f
pyobject_alloc;_PyObject_GC_Malloc+0x2a
PyEval_EvalFrameEx;_PyEval_EvalFrameDefault+0x4b
redwood.runtime.scheduler;process_one_batch+0xab
redwood.runtime.kernel_selector;select_kernel+0x7c
```

alex: flamegraph shows a big yellow wedge for _tokenize_bytes and PyEval_EvalFrameDefault — GIL holding during tokenizer decode path.

perf-bot: nsys trace available: gs://redwood-profiling/2165432199/nsys_trace.qdrep (120s). NVTX regions: kernel_select, batch_assemble, kv_cache_lookup.

maria: So the kernel choice triggers more Python work before GPU enqueue? That matches batching heuristics change that does extra checking for long-seq kernels.

dave: I replayed with perfetto and saw scheduler wakeups spike (sched_wakeup_count +2.5x) in the warmup case. Looks like our pre-checks call into Python to deserialize token meta.

sam: any short-term mitigations? revert warmup heuristics for short-request paths? or move expensive checks off the hot path into a background preparer thread?

alex: I prototyped moving kernel pre-validation into C extension (minimal GIL hold) and it drops tokenization CPU by ~8%. Patch:

```
// pseudo
static PyObject* prevalidate_kernel(PyObject *self, PyObject *args) {
   // parse minimal metadata without creating Python objects
   // return boolean
}
```

alex: But that's more invasive. For 0.32 I'd prefer a config toggle: keep old fast-path for requests < 64 tokens. Rollout to internal Dedicated first.

maria: Agreed. Also add a perf test that runs 1k short requests and captures perf+flamegraph in CI (baseline vs new heuristics).

dave: I'll add a presubmit perf job that uses perf stat + perf script to collect stacks. We should also capture KV cache hit/miss buckets — the cold-start case tends to miss and triggers extra Python handling.

sam: Good call. Can we also add a tiny integration test that simulates tokenization GC pressure? The PyObject_GC_Malloc hits are suspicious.

alex: yes — I'll add a small harness that feeds synthetic short prompts at 200 qps, measure 95p latency and CPU.

alex: Next steps I propose: 1) toggle fallback for <64 tokens, 2) add perf CI + test harness, 3) prototype C prevalidate to land later, 4) verify KV cache prefetch behavior doesn't call into Python on miss.

maria: assign items?

dave: I'll own perf CI + KV cache instrumentation.

sam: I'll prototype C prevalidate and run microbenchmarks.

alex: I'll add the toggle and the harness. I'll post the perf script + full flame SVG to the thread later. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: note: recorded perf stat summary: cycles: 1.2e10, context-switches: 4.3e5, cpu-migrations: 1200, page-faults: 900.

alex: thanks all — keeping this in the open thread for trace links and diffs. If anyone wants the nsys slices I can share access.

maria: thanks — let's aim to have the toggle PR by EOD tomorrow and perf CI by Friday. :rocket:
